item.content:encoded:
Applications are open for the Innovate Africa Challenge 2026 (3rd Edition), a major continental innovation initiative jointly organized by Smart Africa and the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) to accelerate the deployment of Artificial Intelligence solutions that address agricultural and climate challenges across Africa.

Under the theme “From Ideation to Deployment,” the third edition marks an important shift from developing promising technological concepts toward deploying practical, scalable, and context-validated AI solutions capable of delivering measurable benefits to African farmers.

The Innovate Africa Challenge 2026 is specifically seeking startups, innovators, and solution developers working on AI-driven solutions for climate-smart agriculture. The selected solution will move beyond experimentation or pilot-stage development and be deployed within a Smart Africa Member State in collaboration with relevant government ministries, the Smart Africa Secretariat, FAO country offices, and technical experts.

The challenge focuses particularly on AI applications for precision agriculture, crop yield forecasting, pest and disease surveillance, climate risk modelling, adaptive agricultural decision-making, and water and natural resource optimization.

Importantly, this edition is geographically targeted. Applications are only open to eligible applicants from Ghana, Kenya, Malawi, Rwanda, and Uganda.

Innovate Africa Challenge 2026 at a Glance

Key details of the third edition include:

  • Organizers: Smart Africa and the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)
  • Edition: Third Edition
  • Theme: “From Ideation to Deployment”
  • Main Focus: Artificial Intelligence for Climate-Smart Agriculture
  • Eligible Countries: Ghana, Kenya, Malawi, Rwanda, and Uganda
  • Target Applicants: Startups, innovators, and solution developers
  • Geographic Focus: Africa
  • Main Objective: Deploy a proven and scalable AI-driven agricultural solution in a Smart Africa Member State
  • Priority Areas: Precision agriculture, crop forecasting, pest and disease surveillance, climate risk modelling, decision support, and natural resource optimization
  • Application Deadline: No application deadline is stated in the information provided

About the Innovate Africa Challenge

The Innovate Africa Challenge is a continental initiative created to advance technological innovation and accelerate the practical application of solutions capable of addressing major development challenges across Africa.

The third edition is jointly organized by Smart Africa and FAO and concentrates on one of the continent’s most important intersections: Artificial Intelligence, agriculture, food systems, and climate resilience.

Africa’s agricultural sector faces significant and interconnected challenges. At the same time, rapid advances in Artificial Intelligence, digital agriculture, data-driven technologies, and related innovations provide new opportunities to improve agricultural productivity, sustainability, resilience, resource management, and access to markets.

A persistent challenge, however, is moving technological innovations beyond the pilot stage.

Many potentially valuable solutions are developed and tested on a limited scale but are never successfully integrated into national agricultural systems or deployed widely enough to deliver meaningful benefits to farmers.

The Innovate Africa Challenge 2026 seeks to address this gap.

Rather than focusing exclusively on generating new ideas, the third edition emphasizes identifying technologies that have already demonstrated potential and helping move them toward practical deployment and validation.

2026 Theme: “From Ideation to Deployment”

The theme of the third edition is:

“From Ideation to Deployment”

This theme captures the central ambition of the 2026 challenge.

The organizers are seeking to move beyond promising ideas toward solutions that can operate effectively in real agricultural environments.

The challenge therefore places considerable emphasis on technological maturity, practical implementation, contextual relevance, measurable impact, and scalability.

Successful solutions should be capable of producing meaningful outcomes for farmers, agricultural extension services, government institutions, or other stakeholders in African agricultural systems.

Why the Innovate Africa Challenge Matters

Artificial Intelligence has enormous potential to transform African agriculture.

AI-powered agricultural technologies can potentially help farmers and institutions:

  • Make better agricultural decisions
  • Optimize inputs
  • Improve resource efficiency
  • Predict crop yields
  • Detect pests and diseases earlier
  • Respond to climate risks
  • Improve water management
  • Strengthen food security
  • Reduce agricultural losses
  • Improve climate resilience
  • Increase agricultural productivity

Despite this potential, promising innovations frequently struggle to transition from prototypes and pilots to large-scale implementation.

Another challenge identified by the initiative is that innovations are sometimes developed without sufficient validation within the realities of African smallholder farming.

A solution that performs effectively in one technological or agricultural environment may not automatically work in settings characterized by unreliable connectivity, incomplete datasets, diverse languages, different agro-ecological conditions, and predominantly smallholder farming systems.

The third edition of the Innovate Africa Challenge therefore emphasizes deployment and real-world validation.

Building on Previous Innovate Africa Challenge Editions

Previous editions of the Innovate Africa Challenge demonstrated the potential for Artificial Intelligence to contribute to climate action and agriculture.

However, the third edition recognizes that demonstrating technological potential alone is not sufficient.

Many innovations still require deeper validation within African smallholder farming environments before they can achieve widespread adoption and sustainable impact.

The 2026 edition consequently seeks to bridge the gap between innovation and implementation by supporting a solution that can be deployed, validated, and demonstrated under real-world conditions.

Main Objective of the Innovate Africa Challenge 2026

The central objective of the third edition is to identify and support a proven AI-driven solution for climate-smart agriculture and facilitate its deployment within a Smart Africa Member State.

The selected solution is expected to be implemented through collaboration involving:

  • National ministries responsible for Agriculture
  • National ministries responsible for ICT
  • National ministries responsible for Innovation
  • Smart Africa Secretariat
  • FAO country offices
  • FAO technical experts
  • Other relevant ecosystem stakeholders

This collaborative structure is intended to provide the institutional environment required to move an AI solution from a promising innovation toward meaningful implementation.

Expected Outcomes of the Challenge

The Innovate Africa Challenge 2026 is designed to produce three broad outcomes.

1. Deployment of a Scalable and Context-Validated AI Solution

One proven AI-driven solution will be selected, customized to African agricultural realities, deployed, validated, and demonstrated in a real-world setting.

The implementation is expected to contribute to measurable improvements in areas such as:

  • Farmers’ decision-making
  • Agricultural productivity
  • Climate resilience

The deployment should also establish a foundation for potential wider adoption across Smart Africa Member States.

This is an important distinction of the third edition: the challenge is not simply searching for interesting AI ideas. It seeks a solution capable of demonstrating practical value in an authentic agricultural context.

2. Stronger Ecosystem and Multi-Stakeholder Collaboration

The initiative seeks to strengthen collaboration between the various institutions and stakeholders required for successful digital agricultural transformation.

These may include:

  • Technology innovators
  • Government ministries
  • FAO country offices
  • Private-sector organizations
  • Research institutions
  • Farmer organizations
  • Agricultural stakeholders

By connecting these actors, the challenge aims to reduce institutional silos, encourage knowledge exchange, strengthen capacity, and establish an enabling environment for sustained digital transformation in agriculture.

3. Evidence Generation and a Replicable Scale-Up Model

Another important expected outcome is the generation of practical evidence from the deployment process.

Lessons learned from implementation should help create a replicable model for scaling AI-driven climate-smart agriculture solutions across Africa.

Such evidence could contribute to:

  • Policy development
  • Investment decisions
  • Responsible AI adoption
  • Digital agriculture strategies
  • Wider technology deployment
  • Future agricultural innovation programmes

The long-term objective is to amplify the benefits of responsible AI technologies for African farmers and food systems.

Priority Areas for the Innovate Africa Challenge 2026

The challenge identifies several primary areas of interest.

1. Precision Agriculture and Input Optimization

Solutions may use AI and data-driven technologies to help farmers make more precise decisions about agricultural inputs and resources.

The objective is to improve resource efficiency while reducing negative environmental impacts.

Potential applications could support better agricultural decision-making around the use and allocation of farm resources.

2. Crop Yield Prediction and Forecasting

The challenge is interested in AI solutions capable of supporting crop yield prediction and agricultural forecasting.

Improved forecasting can contribute to:

  • Proactive agricultural planning
  • Better decision-making
  • Food security
  • Risk management

Reliable predictions can help farmers, governments, and agricultural institutions anticipate challenges and make more informed decisions.

3. Pest and Disease Surveillance, Detection and Early Warning

Pests and diseases can cause substantial agricultural losses.

The challenge therefore welcomes AI solutions that strengthen:

  • Surveillance
  • Detection
  • Early-warning capabilities
  • Timely agricultural responses

Earlier identification can allow farmers and agricultural institutions to respond before problems become more widespread.

4. Climate Risk Modelling and Adaptive Decision Support

Climate variability and extreme weather conditions increasingly affect agricultural production.

AI technologies capable of modelling climate risks and providing adaptive decision support can help strengthen farmers’ resilience to climate-related shocks.

The challenge seeks solutions capable of translating climate and agricultural information into actionable guidance.

5. Water and Natural Resource Optimization

Efficient management of water and other natural resources is essential to sustainable agriculture.

AI-powered solutions that improve resource optimization therefore fall within the challenge’s priority areas.

Deployment and Validation Requirements

The Innovate Africa Challenge places strong emphasis on technologies capable of operating within actual African agricultural conditions.

Participating startups are expected to demonstrate that their solutions can generate reliable and actionable outputs for one or more of the following:

  • Farmers
  • Agricultural extension services
  • Agricultural institutions

Solutions should be capable of functioning effectively within challenging and diverse environments.

Solutions Must Address African Agricultural Realities

The proposed technology should demonstrate its ability to operate in environments characterized by several important realities.

Smallholder and Informal Farming Systems

Smallholder farmers constitute an important part of African agriculture.

Solutions should therefore be relevant to farming environments that may differ substantially from highly industrialized agricultural systems.

Partial or Low-Frequency Data

AI solutions often depend on large amounts of high-quality data.

However, agricultural data in some settings may be:

  • Partial
  • Incomplete
  • Irregular
  • Collected at low frequency

Solutions should demonstrate an ability to operate effectively under these constraints.

Mobile-First and Low-Connectivity Environments

Digital solutions intended for African farmers should account for differences in connectivity and technology access.

The challenge specifically recognizes environments where mobile devices may be the primary digital platform and internet connectivity may be limited.

Multilingual and Heterogeneous Data Environments

Africa is characterized by significant linguistic, cultural, agricultural, and data diversity.

Proposed technologies should therefore demonstrate an ability to function in multilingual and heterogeneous data environments where appropriate.

Diverse Agro-Ecological Zones and Farming Practices

Agricultural conditions differ significantly across countries and regions.

Solutions should be capable of adapting to diverse:

  • Agro-ecological zones
  • Cropping systems
  • Farming practices
  • Environmental conditions

Integration with National Systems

The challenge is particularly interested in solutions capable of integration with:

  • National agricultural extension systems
  • Government ministry systems
  • Existing agricultural institutions

This integration component is crucial to moving innovations beyond isolated pilots toward broader institutional adoption.

Who Can Apply for the Innovate Africa Challenge 2026?

The challenge is open to:

  • Startups
  • Innovators
  • Solution developers

Applicants must be actively developing or deploying AI-driven solutions for climate-smart agriculture.

The challenge is not solely evaluating the technical sophistication of applicants.

Applicants are also expected to demonstrate:

  • Technological maturity
  • Commitment to strengthening the innovation ecosystem
  • Potential for measurable impact
  • Viable pathways toward scaling
  • Financial sustainability

Click HERE to submit your application

Eligible Countries

The Innovate Africa Challenge 2026 is specifically restricted to applicants from five African countries:

  1. Ghana
  2. Kenya
  3. Malawi
  4. Rwanda
  5. Uganda

The source explicitly states that the call is only open to applicants coming from these countries.

Applicants outside these five countries should therefore not assume eligibility for this particular edition based solely on the challenge’s broader continental objectives.

Additional Eligibility Criteria

The source provided introduces a section stating that applicants must meet additional criteria, but the actual criteria following that heading are not included in the supplied information.

Prospective applicants should therefore carefully review the complete official challenge documentation before submitting an application to confirm all organizational, technical, operational, financial, or other eligibility requirements.

Responsible AI, Data Protection and Governance Requirements

All participating startups must comply with important principles governing data use and Artificial Intelligence.

Data Protection and Privacy

Participants must comply with applicable data protection and privacy requirements in the countries where they operate.

Responsible and Explainable AI

Solutions must apply responsible and explainable AI practices appropriate to agricultural decision-making.

This is particularly important where AI-generated recommendations could influence farmers’ production decisions, resource allocation, or livelihoods.

Bias Identification and Mitigation

Participating startups must demonstrate approaches for identifying and mitigating AI bias.

Particular attention should be given to bias related to:

  • Gender
  • Geography
  • Farming systems

Farmer Data Rights

Participants must respect the rights of farmers whose data may be collected or processed.

Appropriate consent must be obtained for data use.

Confidentiality

All information shared under the challenge must be treated in accordance with applicable confidentiality requirements.

Smart Africa also reserves the right to establish and enforce additional requirements relating to:

  • Data governance
  • Responsible AI
  • Information management

throughout the challenge.

Intellectual Property Rules

Participating startups will retain ownership of their pre-existing intellectual property.

This means intellectual property developed before participation in the challenge remains with the relevant participant.

However, the source establishes additional provisions concerning outputs developed under the initiative.

Smart Africa will retain rights over:

  • Challenge outputs
  • Reports
  • Frameworks developed under the initiative

Any subsequent scale-up or deployment phase may be governed through separate contractual arrangements.

Those agreements may establish specific terms covering:

  • Ownership
  • Licensing
  • Deployment rights

Applicants should therefore review all intellectual property and contractual conditions carefully before participating.

Collaboration with Governments and FAO

A significant feature of the challenge is the planned collaboration between innovators and institutional stakeholders.

The selected solution is expected to be implemented alongside relevant national ministries, Smart Africa, and FAO.

This structure can help ensure that the technology is not developed separately from the institutions responsible for agricultural policy and implementation.

It also provides an opportunity to test whether an innovation can integrate into existing national systems and respond effectively to local agricultural priorities.

Why Scalability Matters

The ultimate goal extends beyond deploying a single solution in one location.

The challenge aims to demonstrate an approach that could provide a foundation for broader adoption across Smart Africa Member States.

A successful solution should therefore have the potential to:

  • Adapt to different agricultural environments
  • Serve larger numbers of farmers
  • Integrate with national systems
  • Demonstrate measurable benefits
  • Operate sustainably
  • Support evidence-based policy and investment
  • Provide a model that could be replicated elsewhere

Why Startups and AI Innovators Should Consider Applying

For startups developing AI solutions for African agriculture, one of the greatest challenges can be moving from product development to meaningful deployment.

The Innovate Africa Challenge directly addresses this transition.

The selected innovation will have an opportunity to demonstrate its capabilities within a real-world environment and work within a multi-stakeholder ecosystem involving government institutions, international organizations, researchers, farmer organizations, and other relevant actors.

For an eligible startup with a mature solution, this provides an opportunity to demonstrate that its technology can generate practical value under African agricultural conditions.

Application Deadline

The information supplied for the Innovate Africa Challenge 2026 states August 31, 2026 as the application deadline.

Click HERE to submit your application

Important Considerations Before Applying

Prospective applicants should carefully assess whether their solutions align with the challenge before submitting an application.

Applicants should be prepared to demonstrate:

  1. A clear AI component within their solution.
  2. Direct relevance to climate-smart agriculture.
  3. Evidence of technological maturity.
  4. Practical value for farmers, extension services, or agricultural institutions.
  5. Ability to operate under real African agricultural conditions.
  6. Potential for measurable impact.
  7. Potential for scaling.
  8. A pathway toward financial sustainability.
  9. Responsible and explainable AI practices.
  10. Compliance with data protection and farmer data rights.
  11. Ability to address potential bias.
  12. Relevance to one or more of the challenge’s priority agricultural areas.

Applicants should also carefully examine the complete official documentation because some detailed eligibility criteria referenced by the source are not included in the information provided.

Visit HERE to learn more about the Innovate Africa Challenge 2026.

Conclusion

The Innovate Africa Challenge 2026 (3rd Edition) represents an important opportunity for AI startups, innovators, and technology developers seeking to transform African agriculture through practical, scalable, and responsible Artificial Intelligence solutions.

Jointly organized by Smart Africa and the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations, the challenge moves beyond the traditional innovation competition model by emphasizing real-world deployment. Under the theme “From Ideation to Deployment,” the initiative seeks one proven AI-driven solution that can be customized, deployed, validated, and demonstrated within African agricultural realities.

The challenge is particularly focused on precision agriculture and input optimization, crop yield prediction and forecasting, pest and disease surveillance, climate risk modelling, adaptive decision support, and water and natural resource optimization.

Solutions must also demonstrate their relevance to the realities faced by African agriculture, including smallholder farming systems, incomplete datasets, low-connectivity environments, multilingual contexts, diverse agro-ecological conditions, and integration with government and agricultural extension systems.

Only applicants from Ghana, Kenya, Malawi, Rwanda, and Uganda are eligible under the geographic restriction stated in the call. Eligible startups and innovators developing mature AI-powered climate-smart agriculture solutions should carefully review the full application requirements, responsible AI principles, data governance provisions, and intellectual property conditions before applying.

With its emphasis on deployment, government collaboration, evidence generation, scalability, and measurable farmer impact, the Innovate Africa Challenge 2026 provides a potentially significant platform for innovators seeking to move promising agricultural AI technologies from pilots toward wider adoption across Africa.

item.content:encoded:
Young people across Europe have an exciting opportunity to become part of one of the continent’s most influential youth policy initiatives. The German-Baltic Future Foundation (DBJW) has officially opened applications for the Youth Ambassador Programme at the 8th German-Baltic Conference, which will take place in Tallinn, Estonia, from 15–18 October 2026.

The conference offers motivated young Europeans an opportunity to engage in high-level policy discussions, collaborate with fellow changemakers, develop policy recommendations for European institutions, and potentially present their work directly to Members of the European Parliament (MEPs) in Brussels.

Unlike many youth conferences, participants will not simply attend presentations—they will actively contribute to developing practical policy proposals addressing some of Europe’s most pressing challenges.

Applications are open until 2 August 2026 (23:59 CEST).

About the German-Baltic Conference

The German-Baltic Conference is an international youth policy conference organized by the German-Baltic Future Foundation (DBJW). The conference brings together young people from across Europe who are interested in democracy, European cooperation, leadership, security, public policy, and civic participation.

The conference creates a platform where participants exchange ideas, debate current European challenges, and jointly create policy recommendations intended for European decision-makers.

Rather than functioning as a traditional academic event, the conference emphasizes collaboration, practical problem-solving, and youth participation in shaping Europe’s future.

Conference Theme 2026: Self-Determination

The central theme for the 2026 conference is:

Self-Determination

Participants will explore what self-determination means for Europe in today’s rapidly changing geopolitical landscape.

The discussions will revolve around three major policy clusters, each addressing a different dimension of Europe’s resilience, democracy, and future.

Conference Policy Clusters

Cluster A: Total Defence and Preparedness

Head of Cluster: Jonas Hoppe

This policy group examines how European societies can strengthen their resilience against crises through comprehensive preparedness.

Key discussion areas include:

  • Total defence strategies
  • Crisis preparedness
  • Civilian and military cooperation
  • National resilience
  • Political leadership
  • Public support for defence strategies
  • European security cooperation
  • NATO and EU coordination
  • Local, national, and European crisis responses

Participants will examine how societies can preserve their ability to make independent decisions during emergencies while strengthening democratic resilience.

Cluster B: Countering Disinformation

Head of Cluster: Maisa Mattila

Disinformation has become one of the greatest threats facing democratic societies.

This cluster focuses on:

  • Combating fake news
  • Fighting online misinformation
  • Addressing foreign information manipulation
  • Protecting democratic institutions
  • Building media literacy
  • Strengthening digital resilience
  • Supporting young people against manipulation
  • Creating community-based responses to disinformation

Participants will work together to develop practical policy recommendations that empower young Europeans to recognize and counter misleading information.

Cluster C: EU Enlargement—Seizing the Momentum

Head of Cluster: Yulia Dziuba

European enlargement has regained strategic importance due to evolving geopolitical realities.

This cluster explores:

  • EU enlargement policy
  • European integration
  • Candidate country accession
  • Democratic governance
  • Security cooperation
  • Institutional readiness
  • Sustainable expansion of the European Union
  • Peacebuilding across Europe

Participants will discuss practical recommendations for improving the EU enlargement process while ensuring both current and future member states are prepared for a stronger European Union.

What Will Youth Ambassadors Do?

Selected Youth Ambassadors will become active contributors throughout the entire programme.

Participants will:

  • Join one policy cluster
  • Attend weekly online preparation sessions
  • Learn policy paper writing
  • Collaborate with experts and fellow participants
  • Participate in policy discussions
  • Draft policy recommendations
  • Exchange ideas with young Europeans
  • Develop leadership and teamwork skills
  • Expand their understanding of European affairs
  • Build an international professional network

Some participants may also be selected to present their completed policy papers before Members of the European Parliament in Brussels in December 2026.

Three Phases of the Programme

The programme is designed as a multi-stage learning experience.

Phase 1: Online Preparation

Beginning in September, participants will attend weekly online meetings where they will:

  • Meet fellow Youth Ambassadors
  • Learn about their policy topic
  • Receive guidance from their Head of Cluster
  • Develop research skills
  • Learn policy drafting techniques

Phase 2: Conference in Tallinn

From 15–18 October 2026, participants will travel to Tallinn, Estonia.

During the conference they will:

  • Participate in intensive workshops
  • Discuss policy challenges
  • Collaborate with international peers
  • Begin drafting policy recommendations
  • Engage in networking sessions

Phase 3: Policy Development

Following the conference, participants will continue collaborating online to:

  • Finalize their policy paper
  • Refine recommendations
  • Prepare presentations
  • Potentially participate in a parliamentary hearing in Brussels

Completed policy papers will be distributed to policymakers at:

  • European Parliament
  • European Union institutions
  • National governments
  • Local decision-makers
  • DBJW partner networks

Benefits of Becoming a Youth Ambassador

Participants will receive numerous academic, professional, and networking benefits, including:

  • Opportunity to influence European policy discussions
  • Direct engagement with European policymakers
  • International networking with young leaders
  • Policy writing experience
  • Leadership development
  • Teamwork and collaboration experience
  • Public policy exposure
  • Practical understanding of European governance
  • International conference participation
  • Enhanced communication skills
  • Exposure to European democratic processes
  • Cross-cultural exchange
  • Potential opportunity to present policy papers in Brussels

Financial Support

The conference organizers provide significant financial support for participants.

Support includes:

  • Accommodation in shared double rooms
  • Catering throughout the conference
  • Partial travel reimbursement

Travel compensation includes:

Participants from:

  • Estonia
  • Latvia
  • Lithuania

Receive up to €100 in travel reimbursement.

Participants from the rest of Europe

Receive up to €200 in travel reimbursement.

Participation Fee

Participants contribute a reduced participation fee based on their country of residence.

€50 participation fee

Applicable to applicants residing in:

  • Estonia
  • Latvia
  • Lithuania
  • Poland
  • Czechia
  • Slovakia
  • Ukraine
  • Slovenia
  • Hungary
  • Croatia
  • Serbia
  • Bosnia and Herzegovina
  • Kosovo
  • North Macedonia
  • Albania
  • Romania
  • Bulgaria
  • Moldova
  • Georgia
  • Armenia
  • Türkiye

€100 participation fee

Applicable to participants living in all other European countries.

Applicants experiencing financial hardship are encouraged to contact the organizers, as financial barriers should not prevent participation.

Who Can Apply?

Applicants must meet the following eligibility requirements:

  • Be between 16 and 30 years old
  • Live in any European country
  • Be fluent in English
  • Be interested in European affairs, leadership, democracy, or policy
  • Be willing to participate in online preparation sessions
  • Be available to attend the conference in Tallinn
  • Be interested in collaborative policy development

Importantly, applicants do not need an academic background.

The organizers explicitly encourage applications from:

  • Young people with non-academic backgrounds
  • Individuals with limited prior knowledge of European politics
  • First-time participants
  • Young people from diverse educational and professional experiences

Application Process

Interested applicants should complete the official online application form before the deadline.

During the application process, candidates are encouraged to:

  • Share original ideas
  • Demonstrate creativity
  • Reflect on personal experiences
  • Avoid relying on AI-generated responses
  • Present authentic perspectives

Originality and independent thinking are strongly valued during the selection process.

Important Dates

  • Applications Open: Currently Open
  • Application Deadline: 2 August 2026 (23:59 CEST)
  • Online Preparation Begins: September 2026
  • Conference Dates: 15–18 October 2026
  • Policy Development Continues: After the conference
  • Potential Parliamentary Hearing in Brussels: December 2026

Why You Should Apply

The Youth Ambassador Programme is far more than a conference. It offers participants the opportunity to become active contributors to discussions shaping Europe’s future. By working alongside peers from across the continent, participants will develop practical policy recommendations addressing security, democracy, information integrity, and European cooperation.

Whether your passion lies in public policy, international relations, civic engagement, journalism, security studies, or leadership, this programme provides valuable experience that can strengthen your academic, professional, and personal development while allowing your voice to be heard by European decision-makers.

Visit HERE for more information about the Youth Ambassador at the 8th German-Baltic Conference 2026 in Estonia.

How to Apply

Interested applicants should complete the official online application before 2 August 2026 (23:59 CEST).

APPLY HERE

Conclusion

The Youth Ambassador Programme at the 8th German-Baltic Conference 2026 is an outstanding opportunity for young people across Europe to develop leadership skills, engage with pressing European policy issues, and contribute meaningful recommendations to influential policymakers. Through a combination of online collaboration, an international conference in Estonia, and the possibility of presenting policy papers in Brussels, participants will gain practical experience, expand their international networks, and play an active role in shaping Europe’s future. If you are passionate about democracy, cooperation, security, or European integration, this programme offers a unique platform to transform your ideas into real policy impact.

item.content:encoded:
Organizations working to create employment opportunities for young people and women now have an exciting opportunity to secure funding through the Blue Ambition Fund (BAF) 2026 Call for Applications. Managed by the Blue Ambition Fund, which is part of the Wilde Ganzen Foundation in the Netherlands, this funding opportunity seeks to empower organizations that are committed to promoting economic independence, strengthening small businesses, and creating sustainable employment opportunities for marginalized communities.

The Blue Ambition Fund supports non-profit organizations and social enterprises that are implementing innovative solutions to address youth unemployment, promote entrepreneurship, and strengthen local economies. Through this open call, eligible organizations from Uganda, Ethiopia, and South Africa are invited to submit concept notes and organizational information for consideration.

If your organization is working to improve livelihoods through skills development, business support, entrepreneurship, or employment creation, this funding opportunity could provide the resources needed to expand your impact.

About the Blue Ambition Fund

The Blue Ambition Fund (BAF) is an initiative of the Wilde Ganzen Foundation, a Netherlands-based organization that works with local partners around the world to support sustainable development initiatives.

The Fund is committed to increasing economic independence among marginalized youth aged 15–35 years and women by investing in organizations that create meaningful employment opportunities and strengthen local businesses.

Rather than offering direct funding to individuals, the Blue Ambition Fund invests in organizations capable of delivering long-term, sustainable employment outcomes within their communities.

The Fund believes that empowering young people and women economically contributes to stronger communities, reduced poverty, inclusive growth, and sustainable development.

Objectives of the Blue Ambition Fund 2026 Call

The 2026 funding round focuses on supporting projects that deliver measurable improvements in employment and entrepreneurship.

Specifically, the Fund seeks organizations that can contribute to the following priorities:

1. Strengthening Small and Growing Businesses

The Blue Ambition Fund aims to support organizations that help Small and Growing Businesses (SGBs) increase their capacity and competitiveness.

Successful projects should focus on:

  • Building business capacity
  • Improving productivity
  • Supporting business growth
  • Strengthening entrepreneurship
  • Expanding market opportunities
  • Creating sustainable and dignified jobs

Organizations should demonstrate how their interventions will contribute to long-term business development while generating employment opportunities for young people and women.

2. Creating Sustainable Employment Opportunities

The second priority area focuses on helping young people and women gain meaningful employment through workforce development initiatives.

Eligible projects may include:

  • Technical skills training
  • Vocational skills development
  • Soft skills training
  • Career coaching
  • Employment readiness programmes
  • Job placement initiatives
  • Workforce development programmes

A key requirement is collaboration with the private sector to ensure that training leads directly to sustainable wage employment.

The Blue Ambition Fund places strong emphasis on programmes that move beyond training alone by guaranteeing or facilitating real employment opportunities for participants.

Who Can Apply?

The Blue Ambition Fund is seeking applications from:

  • Non-profit organizations
  • Social enterprises

Applicants should have missions that align with the objectives of the Blue Ambition Fund, particularly those focused on youth employment, women’s economic empowerment, entrepreneurship, workforce development, and sustainable livelihoods.

Before applying, organizations are strongly encouraged to review the Fund’s participation guidelines to determine whether they meet all eligibility requirements.

APPLY HERE

Countries Eligible for the 2026 Call

The current funding round is only open to organizations operating in the following countries:

  • Uganda
  • Ethiopia

November 2026 – January 2027

Prepare a Concept Note.

Submit both documents before the deadline.

to:

Youth unemployment remains one of the greatest development challenges across many African countries. At the same time, women continue to face barriers to accessing decent employment and entrepreneurship opportunities.

item.content:encoded:
The Institute of Statistical, Social, and Economic Research (ISSER) at the University of Ghana has officially opened applications for its prestigious Pre-Doctoral Fellowship 2026–2027, offering an outstanding opportunity for aspiring researchers who are preparing for doctoral studies. The one-year fellowship is designed to provide talented early-career researchers with extensive hands-on experience in applied development research while working alongside internationally recognized experts in agriculture, natural resources, food systems, and impact evaluation.

Hosted by ISSER under the Standing Panel on Impact Assessment (SPIA) of CGIAR, this fellowship provides participants with the opportunity to contribute to globally significant research projects while developing practical research skills, publishing technical papers, and collaborating with international researchers.

For graduates interested in pursuing a PhD and building a strong research portfolio, this fellowship represents an excellent stepping stone toward an academic or policy-oriented research career.

About the ISSER Pre-Doctoral Fellowship

The ISSER Pre-Doctoral Fellowship is a one-year research programme that aims to strengthen the research capacity of promising scholars before they begin doctoral studies.

The selected Fellow will work under the mentorship of Professor Robert Darko Osei, a member of the Standing Panel on Impact Assessment (SPIA) at the University of Ghana.

Throughout the fellowship period, participants will contribute to research projects focusing on:

  • Agriculture
  • Agricultural development
  • Food systems
  • Natural resources
  • Development economics
  • Impact evaluation
  • Evidence-based policymaking

The programme emphasizes practical research experience through involvement in every stage of the research process—from research planning and design to data collection, statistical analysis, reporting, publication, and dissemination.

Fellowship Details

  • Host Institution: Institute of Statistical, Social, and Economic Research (ISSER), University of Ghana
  • Research Partner: Standing Panel on Impact Assessment (SPIA), CGIAR
  • Duty Station: ISSER, University of Ghana
  • Fellowship Duration: 1 September 2026 – 31 August 2027
  • Programme Length: One year

About ISSER

The Institute of Statistical, Social, and Economic Research (ISSER) is one of Africa’s leading research institutions dedicated to advancing knowledge in economics, development studies, public policy, governance, agriculture, and social sciences.

Operating under the University of Ghana, ISSER conducts policy-relevant research that contributes to national, regional, and global development. The institute collaborates with governments, international organizations, universities, and development partners to generate evidence that informs policy decisions.

Researchers at ISSER frequently engage in multidisciplinary projects addressing Africa’s most pressing development challenges.

About SPIA (Standing Panel on Impact Assessment)

The fellowship is supported through the Standing Panel on Impact Assessment (SPIA) of CGIAR.

SPIA plays a critical role in evaluating the effectiveness and impact of agricultural research investments across the world. Through rigorous evidence generation and impact assessment methodologies, SPIA helps improve agricultural innovations, food security interventions, and sustainable development initiatives.

Fellows joining this programme will have the opportunity to collaborate with researchers working on globally relevant agricultural and development challenges.

Objectives of the Fellowship

The ISSER Pre-Doctoral Fellowship seeks to:

  • Prepare talented researchers for doctoral studies.
  • Build advanced research and analytical skills.
  • Strengthen expertise in development research.
  • Promote evidence-based policy research.
  • Enhance capacity in impact evaluation.
  • Provide exposure to international research collaborations.
  • Encourage publication of high-quality academic research.
  • Develop future leaders in agricultural and development economics.

Fellowship Responsibilities

Successful applicants will become active members of the SPIA research team and will contribute to multiple research activities throughout the fellowship period.

Key responsibilities include:

1. Supporting Scientific Research

The Fellow will assist with:

  • Planning research activities
  • Implementing research projects
  • Monitoring research progress
  • Reporting on activities under the SPIA workplan

2. Research Design and Data Management

Participants will support:

  • Research design
  • Survey preparation
  • Data collection
  • Data management
  • Data cleaning
  • Quantitative data analysis

This provides valuable practical experience in the complete research cycle.

3. International Collaboration

The Fellow will collaborate with:

  • SPIA’s global research team
  • International researchers
  • Other SPIA Panel Members

Such collaborations provide exposure to international research standards and multidisciplinary teamwork.

4. Participation in Research Seminars

Throughout the fellowship, participants will:

  • Attend SPIA monthly research seminars
  • Participate in collaborative research meetings
  • Engage in academic discussions
  • Learn from internationally recognized researchers

5. Research Communication

The Fellow will contribute to producing:

  • Technical reports
  • Research presentations
  • Policy briefs
  • Academic outputs
  • Other scientific communication materials

6. Academic Publications

An important component of the fellowship is scholarly publishing.

The selected Fellow is expected to:

  • Contribute to research publications.
  • Produce at least two technical papers during the fellowship period.

This publication experience significantly strengthens future PhD applications and academic careers.

7. Administrative Support

Additional responsibilities include:

  • Providing project support
  • Assisting with administrative tasks
  • Performing other duties assigned by the SPIA Member

Benefits of the Fellowship

The ISSER Pre-Doctoral Fellowship offers numerous professional and academic advantages.

Participants will benefit from:

  • One year of intensive research experience.
  • Mentorship from experienced researchers.
  • Collaboration with international experts.
  • Participation in global research initiatives.
  • Exposure to advanced quantitative research methods.
  • Experience in impact evaluation.
  • Opportunities to publish technical papers.
  • Participation in monthly research seminars.
  • Development of professional research skills.
  • Strengthened preparation for doctoral studies.
  • Networking opportunities with international researchers.
  • Competitive fellowship remuneration based on qualifications and experience.

Fellowship Remuneration

ISSER will offer the selected Fellow a competitive fellowship package, with remuneration determined according to the Fellow’s qualifications and experience.

Eligibility Requirements

Applicants must satisfy the following requirements:

Academic Qualifications

Applicants should possess:

  • A Master’s degree in Economics, Agricultural Economics, or a related discipline.

Technical Skills

Candidates should demonstrate:

  • Strong quantitative skills.
  • Excellent analytical abilities.
  • Experience in research methodologies.
  • Experience in data collection.

Research Interests

Applicants should have a genuine interest in:

  • Agriculture
  • Natural resources
  • Food systems
  • Development research in developing countries

Professional Competencies

Successful applicants should possess:

  • Good communication skills.
  • Strong teamwork abilities.
  • Research writing skills.
  • Ability to work collaboratively within multidisciplinary research teams.

Additional Advantage

Knowledge or experience in impact evaluation will be considered an added advantage during the selection process.

Required Application Documents

Applicants must submit the following documents:

  • A cover letter explaining their motivation and suitability for the fellowship.
  • A detailed Curriculum Vitae (CV).
  • Copies of academic certificates.
  • Contact information for two academic referees.

Applicants should ensure that all documents are complete and professionally prepared before submission.

How to Apply

Interested candidates should submit their applications electronically.

Applications should be emailed to:

isser@ug.edu.gh

Use the following email subject line:

Application – Pre-Doctoral Fellowship at ISSER

Applicants are encouraged to submit their applications well before the closing date to avoid last-minute technical issues.

APPLY HERE

Application Deadline

Deadline: Monday, 3 August 2026

Late applications may not be considered. Interested candidates are therefore advised to prepare and submit all required documents before the deadline.

Why You Should Apply

The ISSER Pre-Doctoral Fellowship is more than just a research placement—it is a career development programme designed to prepare future scholars for success in doctoral education and beyond.

Participants will gain invaluable experience in applied development research, receive mentorship from leading academics, contribute to internationally significant research projects, and build a strong publication record. The fellowship also offers opportunities to develop advanced analytical skills, engage with global research networks, and strengthen future applications for PhD programmes and research positions.

For graduates who aspire to become researchers, economists, policy analysts, or development professionals, this fellowship provides an exceptional foundation for long-term academic and professional success.

Visit HERE for information about the ISSER Pre-Doctoral Fellowship 2026–2027 at the University of Ghana.

Conclusion

The ISSER Pre-Doctoral Fellowship 2026–2027 offers an exceptional opportunity for early-career researchers to develop practical research expertise while working with one of Africa’s leading research institutions. Through mentorship, international collaboration, publication opportunities, and hands-on experience in development research, Fellows will be well-positioned for future doctoral studies and careers in academia, policy, and international development.

If you have a strong background in economics or a related discipline and are passionate about agriculture, food systems, natural resources, and impact evaluation, this fellowship could be the ideal next step in your academic journey. Be sure to prepare your application carefully and submit all required documents before Monday, 3 August 2026.

For more global Fellowship opportunities, visit OFY HERE
